message:
release: 0.2.128 -- a window that stops answering costs one preview, not the session

One line changes: the version literal. Product 1, tests 0, docs 0. This is the freeze commit and
the release source -- the binaries are built from here.

What it carries. On 2026-09-15 a preview of one window held the host's only control dispatcher for
1h50m, and every session on that machine failed for the duration: connect, first pong, window
list, picker, then fifteen seconds of nothing. The capture now runs in GNLinkCapture with a one
second deadline, the helper is ended when it misses, and the window is skipped for a minute after
three failures. Measured against a real dispatcher with a helper that never answers: the thumbnail
is answered in 1051ms and the next ping comes back in 0ms.

A process rather than a thread, for a reason that was measured rather than assumed.
PW_RENDERFULLCONTENT is served from the DWM redirection surface on this OS -- a window that never
returns from WM_PRINT still yields a thumbnail in 24ms and its WM_PRINT counter stays at zero. So
a stuck capture is stuck somewhere no user-mode cancellation reaches, and ending a process is the
only reclamation there is.

It also carries an updater fix that had nothing to do with previews until this work would have made
it common: ownership followed one link and required that parent to own a window, so GNLinkCapture
under GNLinkStream was recognised as nobody's child and an update was abandoned before touching
the disk.

Still unproven, and not claimed: the number on screen. Nothing here has been observed by anyone
looking at an installed build -- the picker evidence is from isolated sessions with test binaries,
and a field [connection-version] log after install is what would settle it.
